test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 11 Feb, 2026 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: As per the Sectoral Composition of workforce in India, 2011, what percentage of the total workforce was engaged in the primary sector?
solution:
The correct answer is __**54.6%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **Census of India 2011**, the **primary sector**, which predominantly includes **agriculture and allied activities**, employed **54.6%** of the total workforce in the country.
 
• This **54.6%** was further divided into two main categories: **cultivators**, who accounted for **24.9%**, and **agricultural labourers**, who accounted for **29.7%** of the workforce.
 
• The **2011** data highlighted a significant dependence on the **primary sector** for livelihood, despite the sector's decreasing contribution to the **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** compared to the secondary and tertiary sectors.
 
• The total number of workers in **India** during the **2011 Census** was recorded at **481.7 million**, showing an increase from the **2001** figures, but maintaining the trend of agriculture being the largest employer.
 
• The **primary sector** in **India** is characterized by a high degree of **informal employment** and serves as the backbone of the rural economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Primary Sector**:

 
 
• This sector involves the **extraction** and **production** of natural resources. It includes activities such as **farming**, **fishing**, **forestry**, and **mining**.
 
• In the context of **India**, it is often referred to as the **agricultural sector** because **agriculture** is the most dominant activity within this category.
 
 
 
• **Secondary Sector**:
 
 
• Commonly known as the **industrial sector**, it involves the **processing** of raw materials into finished goods through **manufacturing** and **construction**.
 
• In **2011**, this sector accounted for approximately **24.3%** of the workforce, reflecting a slow but steady **industrialization** process in the country.
 
 
 
• **Tertiary Sector**:
 
 
• Known as the **service sector**, it provides **services** rather than tangible goods. Examples include **banking**, **education**, **healthcare**, **transportation**, and **information technology (IT)**.
 
• While this sector contributes the **highest share** to **India's GDP** (over **50%**), its share in **employment** was around **26.8%** as per **NSSO** 68th round data (**2011-12**), indicating a mismatch between **income generation** and **job creation**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Structural Transformation**: The shift of the **workforce** from the **primary sector** to the secondary and tertiary sectors is a sign of **economic development**. However, in **India**, this transition has been unique as the **GDP** shifted directly to services, while the **workforce** remained heavily concentrated in **agriculture**.
 
• **Disguised Unemployment**: A major challenge in the **primary sector** is **disguised unemployment**, where more people are working than required, leading to low **marginal productivity**.
 
• **Workforce Participation Rate (WPR)**: In **2011**, the **WPR** for **India** was **39.8%**, with a higher participation rate in **rural areas** (**41.8%**) compared to **urban areas** (**35.3%**).
 
• **Gender Distribution**: A significant portion of the **female workforce** in **India** is engaged in the **primary sector**, often working as **unpaid family labor** or **marginal workers** in rural agricultural fields.
